## p171 — Ruble rates and expectations about Russia

**Edition context:** p171 — Ruble rates and expectations about Russia.

<a id="edition-cases-p171-p171--ruble-rates-and-expectations-about-russia"></a>



**Status:** Earlier raw body reproduced exactly; two extra corrections are implicit in its published ciphertext. **Key:** `Nov7-9`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Norbert, 2017-03-01, comment 20](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852668). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

<a id="edition-cases-p171-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited reconstruction:**

> In Ukraine und Polen Rubel[kurse stark] steigend infolge Bruches zwischen Deutschland und Sowjetregierung und Erwartung der Wiederherstellung Russlands durch Deutschland und Entente.

**Meaning:** The ruble exchange rate is rising sharply in Ukraine and Poland because of the break between Germany and the Soviet government and expectations that Germany and the Entente will restore Russia.

**Notes:** The passage reports a contemporary expectation; it is not a statement that the expected restoration occurred. Baertl's natural `KURSE STARK` adds an `S` to the exact raw `KURSETARK`. All other wording shown here follows the reproduced body, with spaces and punctuation supplied.

## Ruble prices and payments above par: companions to p171 A1

**Sources on this page:** p171 A2, p171 A3.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-ruble-rate-companions-ruble-prices-and-payments-above-par-companions-to-p171-a1"></a>



**Companion source editions: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The second and third parts of the telegram whose first part was read by
**Norbert in 2017** report prices for Tsar rubles in Kiev and Warsaw, then
recommend allowing more than par for `BONS` if necessary. They complete
the subject of the earlier first-part reading without changing its priority
or its source accounting. The second part requires a substantial, explicitly
conditional layout reconstruction; the third part needs only two printed
erasure fills.

The source is Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p171 A2–A3, PDF page 174](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [three-part section](../../experiments/ruble_rate_companions/sources/p171_A.png)
is headed:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
9th NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) COS v NKJ (1.58 a.m., November 10th)
COS POT FUR GENERAL VON KRESS 1425 (9/11) 3 TLE
```

</details>

Only A2 and A3 are new physical source records in this package. A1 remains
in [the canonical challenge case](#edition-cases-p171), credited to Norbert, with
Max Baertl's later editorial `KURSE STARK` separately identified.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-ruble-rate-companions-a2-what-the-telegram-reports-about-ruble-prices"></a>

### A2: what the telegram reports about ruble prices

Under the conditional layout described below, the direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 252-slot layout after two group exclusions and one added slot:**

```text
GEMEINS0MXXINKIEWXKIEWW?RDENFUERHUNDERTZAYENRUBEL?UNDERTVIERZIGMARKGEZAHLTXINWARSCHAUSO2LENBISHUNDERTNEUNZINMAR?GEZAHATWE?XENX
```

</details>

Six observed-coordinate substitutions, three fills of retained printed
dashes, and one fill of the added unknown coordinate give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional layout, with observed substitutions and separately priced fills:**

```text
GEMEINSAMXXINKIEWXKIEWWURDENFUERHUNDERTZARENRUBELHUNDERTVIERZIGMARKGEZAHLTXINWARSCHAUSOLLENBISHUNDERTNEUNZIGMARKGEZAHLTWERDENX
```

</details>

The opening `GEMEINSAM` continues A1's reference to Germany and the Entente.
The message reports that **140 marks were paid for 100 Tsar rubles in Kiev**,
and that **up to 190 marks were reportedly being paid in Warsaw**. These
amounts are spelled out as words, so they do not require filling the period
key's unknown digit cells. They remain reports made by this telegram, not
independently verified market-price observations. The repeated `KIEW` is
preserved.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-ruble-rate-companions-the-source-is-261-slots-the-working-frame-is-252"></a>

#### The source is 261 slots; the working frame is 252

The [source crop](../../experiments/ruble_rate_companions/sources/p171_A2.png)
prints `RICHI-252`, but its literal transcription contains **261 slots**.
The adopted model makes three explicit layout decisions:

1. Exclude source group 6, **`---DD`**, at positions 25–29.
2. Exclude the visibly struck-through source group 19, **`G-VFA`**, at
   positions 90–94.
3. Add one unknown coordinate within the four-character group **`DVAX`**, at
   source positions 200–203, to make a five-coordinate group.

All indices here are zero-based. Both excluded groups remain visible in the
literal transcript. Their ten slots include **six observed coordinates and
four printed erasures**. The `G-VFA` cancellation is visible; excluding
`---DD` is a further model decision and is not claimed to be uniquely
required by the typography. The source itself does not certify the added
coordinate's exact boundary.

With those two exclusions held fixed, the verifier examines **all five
boundaries** in `DVAX`:

| Source boundary for the added unknown | Known-coordinate substitutions for the full proposed text | Substitutions with places and spelled quantities masked |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 200 | 8 | 6 |
| 201 | 7 | 6 |
| 202 | 6 | 5 |
| 203 | 6 | 5 |
| 204 | 7 | 5 |

The full text has two tied minima, **202 and 203**. Both produce the same
corrected ciphertext, since the supplied `A` can lie before or after an
already observed `A`. The record uses boundary 202 as a representative and
preserves boundary 203 equally. Removing the place and quantity words from
the stencil leaves **three** ties, 202–204. This is a local check of a model
selected after the earlier readable candidate was seen, not an independent
control or a global proof of the original geometry.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-ruble-rate-companions-a3-authorize-more-than-par-if-necessary"></a>

### A3: authorize more than par if necessary

The third part is source-exact at **152 slots** and has two printed dashes.
Its direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
EMPFEHLEDAHERNOTFALLSFUE?BONSAUCHMEHRALSPARIXPARIB?WILLIGENXXWALLERXWALLERXX
```

</details>

Filling those two dashes, with no observed-coordinate change, yields:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
EMPFEHLEDAHERNOTFALLSFUERBONSAUCHMEHRALSPARIXPARIBEWILLIGENXXWALLERXWALLERXX
```

</details>

The sender, `WALLER` repeated, therefore recommends authorizing more than
par for `BONS` if needed. `Bons` is retained as the message's term; the
edition does not identify a particular issuer or financial instrument.
The duplicated **`PARI X PARI`** is also preserved, without deduplication.

## Newspaper sacks arriving via Orsova

**Sources on this page:** p171 B1, p171 B2.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-newspaper-dispatch-newspaper-sacks-arriving-via-orsova"></a>



**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This two-part telegram tells the **Oberpostdirektion in Breslau** that sacks
of Berlin newspapers arrived yesterday and today via **Orsova**, and asks
for immediate postal dispatch by the same route. It gives priority to two
references, `7?3` and `308`, without spelling out their exact administrative
meaning.

The source is Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p171 B, PDF page 174](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [two parts](../../experiments/newspaper_dispatch/sources/p171_B.png)
have this header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) NKJ v LP (1.01 a.m., November 10th)
1858 (9/11) 2 TLE
```

</details>

The page heading says `9th NOVEMBER, 1918.`; the receiving timestamp is
10 November. Both are retained. The source lengths are exactly 200 and
186 coordinates, using the unchanged published Nov7–9 square and ranks.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-newspaper-dispatch-exact-readings-and-separately-priced-repairs"></a>

<details>

**Raw output:**

```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution repairs `DIREKTIOK→DIREKTION`, and
two fills of printed dashes give:

```

```

<a id="edition-cases-radio-newspaper-dispatch-what-remains-unknown-and-what-an-earlier-hypothesis-would-imply"></a>

### Unresolved postal number and conditional digit assignment

The unknown in `7?3` is **not a printed erasure**. Its two coordinates are
fully observed: source positions **172 and 32** form **`XA`**, one of the two
unassigned cells in the published Nov7–9 square. Its baseline domain is
**`56`**. Both the original and edited ciphertext retain that exact pair.

The earlier [military-context certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json)
separately proposes `VF→6` and consequently `XA→5`, under its independent
French-telegram unit identification. If that existing conditional layer is
adopted, this field becomes **`753`**. The new postal message supplies no
independent confirmation of that digit assignment; `7?3` remains the baseline
reading. No specific field-post office or unit is identified here.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-newspaper-dispatch-attribution-and-verification"></a>

### Attribution and verification

The period key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**. This B telegram is physically separate from the p171 A1
challenge, whose body was read by **Norbert in 2017** and is retained in

The [inputs](../../experiments/newspaper_dispatch/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../../experiments/newspaper_dispatch/certificates.json)

```

## p171 C — Namur order for Staedt to contact HPT V. Weiher; complementary source witness

**Edition context:** The Namur order: two witnesses for Staedt and Weiher.

**Related source pages:** [p172 E](172.md#source-p172-e).

<a id="edition-cases-people-namur-order-witnesses-the-namur-order-two-witnesses-for-staedt-and-weiher"></a>



**Source reconciliation and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two closely related transmissions instruct **Hauptmann Staedt in Namur**
to contact `HPT V. WEIHER` at an Etappen inspection. The latter is to receive
a detailed order by `11 VORM`; the message is signed `MJR KROEGER`.
The witnesses together support this 126-position reading:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — joint witness reconstruction under the stated same-message model:**

```text
HPTMANNSTAEDTNAMURXXBITTESICHMITHPTVXXWEIHERETAPPENINSP1INVERBINDUNGSETZENDERBIS11VORMAUSFUEHRLICHENBEFEHLBEKOMMTXXMJRKROEGERX
```

</details>

The anomalous **`INSP1IN`** and literal **`HPTVXX`** are retained. The
edition does not silently replace the `1` with a separator or insert letters
into the title abbreviation. The source spelling `STAEDT` is retained
without a new biographical identification.

<a id="edition-cases-people-namur-order-witnesses-the-two-physical-sources"></a>

### The two physical sources

Both are in Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view),
and use the unchanged published **Nov10–12** square and ranks.

| Witness | Source | Header | Received slots |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| p171 C | [Printed p171, PDF page 174](../../experiments/namur_order_witnesses/sources/p171_C.png) | `--- v SY (7.26 p.m., November 10th); 1800; RICHI-252` | 252, including four printed dashes |
| p172 E | [Printed p172, PDF page 175](../../experiments/namur_order_witnesses/sources/p172_E.png) | `SY v MAX (7.21 p.m., November 10th); RICHI----; (J'md)` before the received groups | 242, all valid coordinates |

The receiving time on E is five minutes earlier than C's. The edition
preserves both timestamps and does not infer an actual relay sequence.
The p171 page heading is 9 November, while C's own receiving timestamp
explicitly says 10 November.

C's direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
HPTMDNNSTAEDTNAMQRXXBITTESICHMITHPTVXXWEGHERE?AB?ENINSP1?NVERBINDUNGSETZENDE4BIS11VORMAUSFUEHRLICHENBQFE?LBEKOMMTXXMJRKROEGERX
```

</details>

E's earlier OCR stream had only 235 positions and did not yield this
coherent body. Visual retranscription supplies its actual **242 received
coordinates**. Under the same-message model, E is missing ten leading
coordinates, giving this direct reading in a 252-coordinate frame:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional same-message 252-slot frame with ten absent leading coordinates:**

```text
HPTMANN?1AEDTNA?URXXBIT?ESICHJI?HPTVXXW?IHERETA?PENINSP?I?VERBI?DUNGSET?ENDERBI?11VORMAUSFUEHRLICHENBEFEHLBEKOMMRXXPJRKROEGERX
```

</details>

The ten-coordinate leading loss is inferred from the relationship between
the witnesses; E does not display a legible total length or explicitly
count a ten-coordinate gap. It remains a stated model assumption.

<a id="edition-cases-people-namur-order-witnesses-why-the-alignment-is-useful"></a>

### Complementary coordinate evidence

Aligning E's first received coordinate with C source index **10** compares
**238 jointly observed coordinates**: **227 agree** and **11 conflict**.
E supplies observed values for all four printed dashes in C, while C
supplies E's ten modeled missing leading values:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — ten leading coordinates supplied by the other witness:**

```text
DGAAV FADFD
```

</details>

This offset is the unique highest agreement fraction among the **87 relative
offsets with at least 200 jointly observed coordinate pairs**. The comparison
uses ciphertext values, without a language score. It is a finite alignment
check, not a statistical significance claim or a global exclusion of every
possible original length.

The name correction **`WEGHER→WEIHER`** is supported by an observed coordinate
in E, rather than merely by the familiarity of a surname. Conversely, C
supplies correct-looking word and name values where E has other errors.
Lasry et al.'s separate discussion of the neighboring p172 C/p175 A family
also mentions von Weiher; that is retained as prior context, not used to
claim a new identification of the officer in these two witnesses.

<a id="edition-cases-people-namur-order-witnesses-exact-reconciliation-cost-with-the-alternatives-retained"></a>

### Exact reconciliation cost, with the alternatives retained

For two aligned streams to represent one common ciphertext, at least one
observed coordinate must change at each of the **11 conflicts**. The
selected readable body needs exactly **six substitutions in C and five in
E**, meeting that lower bound. Four printed-dash fills in C and ten modeled
prefix fills in E are separately accounted for.

Every coordinate value in the selected common ciphertext is **observed in
at least one witness**. No new coordinate value is supplied solely from a
word guess. The evidence for its plaintext pairs is:

| Complete coordinate pair supporting a selected character | Positions |
| --- | ---: |
| Observed in both witnesses | 102 |
| Observed only in C | 14 |
| Observed only in E | 9 |
| One coordinate supplied by each witness | 1 |
| **Total** | **126** |

The mixed pair is the first `P` in `ETAPPEN`, plaintext position **47**:
C supplies working coordinate 5 and E supplies working coordinate 52.
Thus **125 of 126 whole pairs** are directly observed in one of the two
sources, and the remaining pair is covered coordinate by coordinate.

Minimum cost does not establish a unique original reading. Each conflicting
coordinate has two source-supported choices, yielding **2¹¹ = 2,048**
minimum-cost common coordinate streams under this fixed alignment. The
verifier enumerates all of them, checks the same total cost, and records
their ordered digest. The complete conflict table and selected choice bits
make every alternative reproducible. The readable body is an editorial
choice within that set, with `INSP1IN` left unrepaired.

| Witness | Literal source slots | Analysis-frame slots | Raw fixed labels | Edition labels | Known-coordinate substitutions | Printed fills | Modeled-prefix fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| p171 C | 252 | 252 | 122 / 126 | 126 / 126 | 6 | 4 | 0 |
| p172 E | 242 | 252 | 115 / 126 | 126 / 126 | 5 | 0 | 10 |
| **Total** | **494** | **504** | **237 / 252** | **252 / 252** | **11** | **4** | **10** |

These are two physical witnesses of **one 126-position body**, not two
independent bodies totaling 252 distinct characters. There is no deletion,
source reordering or baseline-key change.

<a id="edition-cases-people-namur-order-witnesses-attribution-and-reproduction"></a>

### Attribution and reproduction

The period key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**. C already appeared as an unreviewed OCR-derived candidate.
The new contribution is the exact source review of both witnesses, the
recovery of E's actual received stream, the joint reconstruction and its

The [inputs](../../experiments/namur_order_witnesses/inputs.json) preserve
all source rows and headers. The
[certificate](../../experiments/namur_order_witnesses/certificates.json)
contains all 87 alignment comparisons, all 11 coordinate conflicts,
character-by-character support, repairs, raw domains and global round-trip
witnesses. Arbitrary key/erasure witnesses certify consistency only.

```sh
python experiments/namur_order_witnesses/verify.py --verify
```

The optional `--pdf` argument verifies the pinned scan and independently
regenerates both source-crop images for pixel comparison.
